subject: Math
title: Frequency Tables
source: Savvas Topic 5, Lesson 5-1 'Collect and Organize Data' (Another Look + Additional Practice, pp. 67–68)
notes: Questions 1–9 from the worksheet are included exactly (Zayla's color survey, favorite subject, picnic food). Question 7: science and reading tie at 6, so Sasha is not exactly right.

lesson.title: What is a frequency table?
lesson.html:
A frequency table shows how many times each choice happens.
We use tally marks to count: four lines, then a slash across makes 5.

lesson.title: Counting tallies
lesson.html:
Count by fives for each group with a slash, then add the extra lines.
Example: two full groups and two extra lines = 5 + 5 + 2 = 12

lesson.title: Zayla's survey
lesson.html: Zayla asked 16 classmates their favorite color. Tap each classmate as you count them, then fill in the table.

lesson.title: Reading tables to answer questions
lesson.html:
How many in all? add every row.
How many more? subtract.
How many did NOT…? add the other rows (or total − that row).

list.q: What does a frequency table show?
list.a: How many times each choice happens
list.why: A frequency table counts how often each choice shows up.

list.q: How many tally marks make one group with a slash?
list.why: Four lines plus a slash across = 5.

list.q: Four lines and a slash across them means…
A table says Red = 3, Blue = 7. What does the 7 tell you?
list.why: The Number column tells how many chose that color.

list.q: How many students chose red or blue as their favorite color?
How many students did NOT choose blue as their favorite color?
How many MORE students chose blue than yellow as their favorite color?
How many students did Zayla survey in all?
How many MORE students chose science than math as their favorite subject?
Sasha said that science was the favorite subject of the most students. Do you agree?
list.a: Not exactly — science and reading are tied at 6
w: Yes — science has the most all by itself
list.why: Science 6 and Reading 6 are tied for the most.
list.hint: Look at the biggest numbers. Is there only one?

list.q: Three more students were surveyed. One chose art and two chose math. What changes in the table?
list.why: Art 5 + 1 = 6. Math 4 + 2 = 6. The total is now 24.
list.hint: Add 1 to art and 2 to math.

list.q: Jorge surveyed his classmates about picnic food. How many students did Jorge survey?
